text: Let (Ω, 𝒜, P) be a probability space. For each i in an arbitrary index set I, let E_i be a measurable space and let X_i : Ω → E_i be a measurable random variable. Assume that the family (X_i)_{i∈I} is jointly independent. Let J be an arbitrary index set, and for each j∈J let S_j be a finite subset of I. Assume S_j ∩ S_k = ∅ whenever j ≠ k. For each j, form the random vector Y_j = (X_i)_{i∈S_j}, taking values in the finite product ∏_{i∈S_j} E_i with its product σ-algebra. Then (Y_j)_{j∈J} is jointly independent. Explicitly, for every finite F⊆J and every choice of measurable B_j⊆∏_{i∈S_j}E_i (j∈F), P(⋂_{j∈F}{Y_j∈B_j}) = ∏_{j∈F}P(Y_j∈B_j). Empty blocks and the empty finite test family are included in the usual product conventions.

scope: Joint independence uses all finite subfamilies of arbitrary index sets. Each coordinate block S_j is finite; the blocks are pairwise disjoint and their random vectors use the product sigma-algebras. The target is the ordinary probability-space theorem with arbitrary, possibly infinite J.
